除了 A 也 B means "besides A, also B".
除了英语，他也会说法语。
Besides English, he can also speak French.
q: Where did Zhang Qian start his journey?
What was taken west along the road?

L.s: Tang poem by Du Mu (public domain)
L.su: Du Mu stops his carriage to admire autumn leaves.
ss: Far up the cold mountain a stone path slants;
where white clouds rise, there are homes.
I stop the carriage, loving the maple grove at dusk;
frost-touched leaves are redder than spring flowers.
q: What are redder than spring flowers?

L.s: Tang poem by Du Mu (public domain)
L.su: Du Mu, walking in drizzle, asks a cowherd where to find wine.
ss: At Qingming time the rain falls in drifting threads;
travellers on the road feel their spirits break.
May I ask where there is a tavern?
The cowherd points far off to Apricot Blossom Village.
q: What does the cowherd point to?

L.s: Tang poem by Wang Wei (public domain)
L.su: Wang Wei sends red beans as a symbol of missing someone.
ss: Red beans grow in the southern land;
how many sprigs sprout when spring comes?
I hope you will gather many,
for these things stir longing most.
q: What do red beans stand for?

L.s: Song poem by Su Shi (public domain)
L.te: Written on the Wall at Xilin Temple
L.su: Su Shi on why we cannot see the mountain while standing in it.
ss: Seen across it is a ridge, from the side a peak;
far, near, high, low — each view differs.
I cannot know Lushan's true face,
only because I am within this mountain.
q: What does the poet say about views?
Why can't he know the true face?
What lesson does the poem suggest?

L.s: Song poem by Su Shi (public domain)
L.te: Drinking by West Lake, Sunny Then Rainy
L.su: Su Shi compares West Lake to the beauty Xi Shi.
ss: Water glitters, best on a sunny day;
mountains hazy, rain is wondrous too.
If I compare West Lake to Xi Shi,
light or heavy make-up always suits her.
q: What does he compare the lake to?

L.s: Tang poem by Meng Jiao (public domain)
L.su: A mother sews a coat for her departing son.
ss: The thread in a loving mother's hand,
the coat on the wanderer's back.
Before he leaves she sews it close and tight,
fearing he will be slow to return.
Who says the heart of a small blade of grass
can repay the spring sun's light?
q: Why does she sew so tightly?
She fears he will return late
What does the grass stand for?

L.s: Tang poem by Du Fu (public domain)
L.su: Du Fu describes the view from his window in spring.
ss: Two orioles sing in the green willows;
a line of white egrets rises into the blue sky.
The window frames the western peaks' snow of a thousand autumns;
the door moors boats that have come ten thousand miles from Wu.

L.s: Tang poem by Zhang Ji (public domain)
L.su: Zhang Ji, sleepless on a boat, hears the temple bell across the water.
ss: The moon sets, crows cry, frost fills the sky;
river maples and fishing lights face my troubled sleep.
Outside Gusu city stands Hanshan Temple;
its midnight bell reaches the traveller's boat.

L.su: A cheerful Han dynasty folk song about fish playing among lotus leaves.
ss: In the south one can pick lotus; how thick the lotus leaves are!
Fish play among the lotus leaves.
Fish play east of the leaves, fish play west of the leaves,
fish play south of the leaves, fish play north of the leaves.
q: What can be picked in the south?

L.s: Tang poem by Li Bai (public domain)
L.te: Seeing Meng Haoran Off at Yellow Crane Tower
L.su: Li Bai watches his friend's sail disappear down the great river.
ss: My old friend takes leave of Yellow Crane Tower to the west;
in the misty flowers of the third month he goes down to Yangzhou.
The lone sail's distant shadow vanishes into blue sky;
I see only the Yangtze flowing to the horizon.
q: What does the poet see at the end?

L.su: A small act of kindness on a rainy evening stays with a woman for years.
ss: The rain started suddenly in the early evening.
She stood at the entrance of a bookshop, gazing at the hazy grey street, hesitating over whether to dash out into the rain.
"Use mine." An unfamiliar voice came from behind her.
A man with glasses held out a black umbrella, his expression calm, as if this were nothing more than the most ordinary of small matters.
She instinctively declined: "What about you?"
"My home is just across the street. Getting rained on for a few steps is nothing." Having said this, he turned and walked into the curtain of rain, and his back soon disappeared into the crowd.
In the many years that followed, she was never able to forget that umbrella, nor that moment when he turned away.
She wasn't sure whether it was love. She only knew that on that rainy day, a kind of warmth had quietly fallen into her life.
g: 把 moves the object before the verb to show what is done to it and where it ends up.
He handed the book to me.
再 + adjective + 不过 means "it can't be more …": the most … there could be.
这是再简单不过的问题。
This is the simplest question imaginable.
仿佛 means "as if / seemingly" and is common in literary writing.
It was as if she heard the sound of rain.
始终 means "all along". 没能 + verb means "was unable to …" despite wanting to.
I was never able to get in touch with him.
q: Where was the woman standing when the rain began?
At the entrance of a bookshop
What did the man say about his home?
It was just across the street
How did he react when she asked, "What about you?"
He said it didn't matter and walked into the rain
He asked to walk with her
How does the woman feel years later?
She never forgot it and is unsure whether it was love

L.su: Everyday habits that reduce our impact on the climate.
ss: Global warming is one of the most severe challenges facing humanity today.
Scientists point out that massive carbon-dioxide emissions are the main cause of climate warming.
Therefore "low-carbon living" is gradually becoming a fashionable lifestyle.
So-called low-carbon living means reducing energy consumption as much as possible in daily life.
For instance, take the subway and buses more when going out, and cycle or walk for short distances.
At home, switch off lights as you leave, unplug appliances not in use, and don't set the air conditioner too low in summer.
Bringing your own shopping bag and using fewer disposable plastics are also good habits.
One person's strength may be limited, but if everyone starts with small things nearby, the combined effect should not be underestimated.
g: 所谓 A，就是 B defines a term: "so-called A means B".
所谓幸福，就是家人平安。
So-called happiness is the safety of one's family.
尽量 means "as much as possible".
Please come as early as you can.
q: What is a main cause of warming?
What should you do with unused appliances?
What does the author say about individuals?

L.su: Ancient thinkers and modern research on what makes a good life.
ss: Happiness is an ancient yet ever-new topic.

Confucians hold that happiness comes from cultivating oneself and fulfilling one's duties to family and society; Daoists advocate following nature, saying that only by desiring nothing can one gain inner peace.
Modern psychological research finds the relationship between money and happiness is not a simple proportion.
Once income meets basic needs, additional wealth does very little to raise happiness.
On the contrary, good relationships, meaningful work and a sense of control over life have a deeper influence on happiness.
A study tracking people for over eighty years shows that those in close contact with family and friends tend to be healthier and live longer.
Clearly, happiness is not far away; it is hidden in everyday moments with others.
Cherishing those in front of us may be the simplest path to happiness.
g: 并非 is a formal "is not at all".
他没有生气，相反很高兴。
He wasn't angry; on the contrary he was happy.
q: What do Confucians say leads to happiness?

L.su: How conservation efforts have helped China's national treasure.
ss: The giant panda is China's national treasure and a symbol of world conservation.
They live mainly in the mountains of Sichuan, Shaanxi and Gansu and feed on bamboo.
An adult panda eats more than ten kilograms of bamboo a day, spending over half of each day eating.
Because forests were felled and bamboo flowered and died over large areas, pandas once faced the danger of extinction.
To protect them, China set up many nature reserves and established special research and breeding centres.
After decades of effort, the number of wild giant pandas has risen to nearly two thousand.
In 2021 the panda's conservation status was lowered from "endangered" to "vulnerable".
However, experts remind us that climate change is still a major threat to pandas, and conservation work cannot be relaxed.
g: 以 A 为 B means "take A as B".
He makes a living by teaching.
由于 gives a formal reason.
由于天气不好，航班取消了。
Because of bad weather, the flight was cancelled.

L.te: The Story of the Forbidden City
L.su: A short history of China's imperial palace in Beijing.
ss: The Forbidden City lies in the heart of Beijing and was the imperial palace of the Ming and Qing dynasties.
It was completed in 1420, and altogether twenty-four emperors lived here and handled affairs of state.
The whole complex covers 720,000 square metres and has more than nine thousand rooms, making it the largest group of ancient palace buildings in the world.
The buildings are strictly arranged along a central axis and are symmetrical on both sides, showing the solemnity of imperial power.
The yellow glazed tiles and red palace walls stand out remarkably under the blue sky.
In 1925 the Forbidden City became a museum, open to ordinary people.
Today more than ten million visitors come every year, and to protect the cultural relics the number of visitors is limited.
Walking into the Forbidden City, people feel as if they are entering the depths of history.
g: 位于 means "to be located in" and is formal.
This city lies on the Yangtze.
为了 + purpose means "in order to".
For his health, he runs every day.
q: Which dynasties used the Forbidden City as their palace?
Why is the number of visitors limited?

L.s: Retelling of a classic idiom story (Han Feizi, public domain)
L.te: Waiting by a Stump for a Hare
L.su: The farmer who waited for luck to repeat.
ss: In the state of Song there was a farmer who toiled in his field every day.
One day a wild hare ran swiftly through the field, accidentally hit the tree stump at its edge, and died on the spot.
The farmer picked up a hare without the slightest effort and was overjoyed.
From then on he had no heart to farm, sitting by the stump all day waiting for another hare to hit it.
Day after day, year after year, no more hares came, and the farmer's fields gradually turned to weeds.
The neighbours all laughed at his foolishness, but he stubbornly kept guarding the stump.
This story tells us not to treat chance success as inevitable, still less to give up effort and wait for luck to arrive.
g: 不费吹灰之力 is a chengyu: "without the slightest effort".
这对他来说不费吹灰之力。
日复一日 means "day after day".
q: It hit a stump and died
It was caught in a trap
What happened to the farmer's fields?
Do not wait for luck to repeat

L.s: Retelling of a classic idiom story (Zhuangzi, public domain)
L.su: A master cook shows how skill comes from understanding.
ss: In the Warring States period a cook named Ding butchered an ox for King Hui of Wei.
Where his hand touched, shoulder leaned, foot trod and knee pressed, there was sound; the blade swished in and out, in time with music.
King Hui exclaimed, "Excellent! How can your skill reach such heights?"
The cook put down his knife: "What I pursue is the Way, which surpasses mere technique.
When I began butchering, all I saw was a whole ox; after three years I no longer saw the whole ox.
Now I meet it with spirit rather than eyes; following the ox's natural structure, my blade roams through the gaps between joints and has room to spare.
A good cook changes knives yearly because he cuts; an average cook monthly because he hacks.
"My knife has served nineteen years and carved thousands of oxen, yet its edge is as if newly ground."
King Hui said, "Hearing you, I have learned the principle of nurturing life."
g: 游刃有余 is a chengyu: "handle with ease".
他处理这些问题游刃有余。
He handles these problems with ease.
q: What did Cook Ding use his knife on?
What did he pursue beyond technique?
How long had his knife lasted?

L.su: China's journey from cash to QR codes.
ss: Walking in Chinese streets you notice an interesting phenomenon: from upscale malls to roadside stalls, nearly everyone pays by phone.
The reason mobile payment spread so quickly is inseparable from its convenience.
Just scan a QR code and a transaction is done in seconds, sparing the trouble of making change and avoiding the risk of carrying lots of cash.
For merchants it lowers operating costs; for consumers it also brings points and discounts.
At the same time, the huge amount of data accumulated gives financial institutions a basis for assessing personal credit.
Yet behind the convenience lie hidden dangers, such as leaks of personal information and online fraud, which occur from time to time.
Some elderly people, unable to use smartphones, have instead met inconvenience in daily spending.
For this reason the government requires merchants to keep cash as an option, ensuring nobody is left behind.
g: 之所以 states the result first: "the reason that ... is because".
他之所以成功，是因为他很努力。
The reason he succeeded is that he worked hard.
与此同时 means "at the same time; meanwhile".
与此同时，另一队也到了。
q: How do people mostly pay in China?
Merchants keep cash as an option

L.su: Two traditions of healing, and how they can work together.
ss: Traditional Chinese medicine has a history of thousands of years, stresses the "unity of heaven and humanity" and sees the body as a whole.
In treating illness it stresses four methods — looking, listening, asking and feeling the pulse — judging a condition from complexion, voice, symptoms and pulse.
Common treatments include herbal medicine, acupuncture, massage and cupping.
By contrast Western medicine puts more weight on scientific experiments and data, uses instruments for tests, and treats specific symptoms.
Western medicine is remarkably effective for emergencies and injuries, but it seems inadequate for some chronic diseases.
Chinese medicine, on the other hand, has unique strengths in regulating the body and preventing disease.
Today more and more hospitals advocate combining the two, drawing on each one's strengths to offset the other's weaknesses.
Whichever method is used, the most important thing is to respect science and life.
g: 相比之下，这里的房租便宜多了。
By comparison, rent here is much cheaper.
无论 A，都 B means "no matter A, B".
无论多忙，他都坚持运动。
q: What is Western medicine strong at?

L.su: How China is adapting to a growing elderly population.
ss: With rising living standards and improving medical care, Chinese life expectancy keeps lengthening and society has entered ageing.
According to statistics, the over-sixties exceed two hundred million, nearly one fifth of the total population.
At the same time the birth rate keeps falling, the labour supply is shrinking and pension funds face great pressure.
The traditional notion of raising children for old-age support is being challenged, since many young people are too busy to care for their parents.
To cope with this, localities are exploring various models of elderly care such as community care, home care and combined medical-and-care.
Many cities have also set up universities for the elderly, giving them chances to learn painting, photography and how to use smartphones.
Experts point out that responding to ageing cannot rely on government alone but needs the joint participation of families, communities and firms.
Letting every elderly person enjoy their later years in peace is an important measure of a society's civilisation.
g: 无暇 is formal for "have no time to".
He has no time to attend to these details.
经济发展了，生活水平也随之提高。
The economy grew, and living standards rose with it.
q: How many Chinese are over sixty?
What do cities provide for the elderly?

L.s: Retelling of a traditional Chinese myth
L.su: The legend behind the Mid-Autumn Festival.
ss: Long, long ago there were ten suns in the sky; they scorched the crops until they withered, and the people suffered terribly.
A hero named Hou Yi was very strong and extremely accurate with his arrows.
He climbed a high mountain and shot down nine suns in one breath, leaving only one to warm the earth.
Later the Queen Mother of the West gave Hou Yi a magic pill; whoever swallowed it would live forever.
Hou Yi could not bear to leave his wife Chang'e, so he gave her the medicine to keep.
One day the wicked Feng Meng took advantage of Hou Yi's absence, broke in and forced Chang'e to hand over the pill.
In desperation Chang'e swallowed it; her body at once grew light and slowly floated into the sky, finally landing on the moon.
When Hou Yi returned he missed his wife terribly.
Every year on the fifteenth of the eighth month he would set out the fruit and mooncakes she loved and make offerings to the moon.
This is the origin of the Mid-Autumn custom of admiring the moon and eating mooncakes.
g: 舍不得 means "can't bear to part with or do".
He can't bear to throw out the old books.
q: Why did Hou Yi shoot down nine suns?
Who gave Hou Yi the magic pill?
The Queen Mother of the West
How does the story explain Mid-Autumn customs?
Hou Yi offered fruit and mooncakes to the moon

L.su: The case for reading old books in an age of short videos.
ss: In an age when short videos take up much of our time, picking up a classic seems a luxury.
Yet classics endure precisely because they have withstood the test of time.
A good classic often crosses time and space to touch what is most essential in human nature — joy, anger, sorrow and delight, love and hatred.
Reading classics not only broadens horizons but sharpens thought: faced with a complex, finely written masterpiece, readers must settle down and chew it over.
This capacity for deep reading is especially precious in an age of fragmented reading.
Of course, reading classics need not seek quick results, nor must you force yourself to like every celebrated work.
You might begin with works that interest you; slowly you'll find that words once obscure become familiar.
Conversing with great souls is itself an incomparable pleasure.
q: They withstood the test of time
Settling down and chewing it over
What does the writer say about enjoyment?
Talking with great souls is incomparable

L.su: An essay on the old streets and shops that quietly hold a city's collective memory.
ss: A city's memory is often not hidden in museums, but scattered in those unremarkable corners.
An old street shaded by plane trees, a tailor's shop that has been open for half a century, or an alley entrance from which the smell of soy milk drifts on some early morning.
However, as the pace of urban renewal keeps quickening, these spaces that carry collective memory are quietly disappearing.
Bulldozers roar past, leaving uniform high-rises behind, yet also wiping out the emotional coordinates shared by several generations.

Some believe this is the price development must pay; others argue that protecting old streets does not mean rejecting modernization, but letting the new and the old coexist harmoniously in the same soil.
How exactly to choose, I'm afraid, has no standard answer.
But we should at least realize that when the last old brick is taken down, what is lost is not only the building itself, but also the soul of a city.
g: 随着 + a change introduces a trend that goes along with the result: "as / along with …".
随着天气变冷，人们穿上了厚衣服。
As the weather gets colder, people put on thick clothes.
意味着 means "to imply / to mean". 并不意味着 corrects a wrong inference: "does not necessarily mean".
努力并不意味着一定成功。
Working hard doesn't necessarily mean success.
"not only … but also …", a bit more formal than 不但…而且….
He is not only smart but also hardworking.
恐怕 expresses a worried guess: "I'm afraid that …", usually about a bad outcome.
I'm afraid it will rain tomorrow.
q: Where does the essay say a city's memory often lies?
In ordinary corners such as old streets and small shops
What is happening to these spaces?
They are being rebuilt exactly as before
According to supporters of preservation, protecting old streets does not mean what?
What is lost when the last old brick is taken down?
The building and also the soul of a city

L.su: China's space programme from Dongfanghong-1 to the space station.
ss: 〇
In 1970 China successfully launched its first artificial satellite, Dongfanghong-1, opening a new chapter in its space programme.
〇〇
In 2003 Yang Liwei flew into space aboard Shenzhou-5, making China the third country after the Soviet Union and the United States to master crewed spaceflight independently.
Since then it has achieved a series of remarkable successes: the Chang'e probe landed on the far side of the Moon, Tianwen-1 reached Mars, and a space station was completed.
Space technology reflects national strength and also drives innovation in materials, communications, medicine and other fields.
Many everyday products, such as navigation systems and non-stick coatings, derive from space technology.
Of course, space exploration needs huge investment and carries great risk.
Some question whether money spent on space is worthwhile, but scientists believe humanity's curiosity about the unknown is the fundamental driver of civilisation's progress.
g: 继 A 之后 means "following A".
继北京之后，上海也推出了新政策。
Following Beijing, Shanghai introduced new policy.
q: When was the first Chinese satellite launched?
What do scientists say drives progress?

L.su: How personalised feeds narrow our view of the world.
ss: Today people have more and more channels for information, yet their horizons have not necessarily widened.
Apps push content users are interested in based on their browsing history, and over time the information people encounter becomes ever more uniform.
Scholars call this the "information cocoon": just as silkworms are wrapped layer upon layer in their own thread, people are confined by their own preferences.
Inside the cocoon, people easily develop an aversion to differing views and even fall into obsession.
More worrying still, algorithms, to attract attention, often amplify emotional speech and lead to the widening tear of social consensus.
To break the cocoon, individuals should first consciously encounter information from different sources, read more, and talk with people of differing views.
Platforms should also shoulder social responsibility, make algorithms more transparent and give users the right to choose.
Only by keeping an open mind can we avoid losing our way in the ocean of information.
g: 久而久之 means "as time passes".
久而久之，他习惯了这里的生活。
Over time, he got used to life here.
唯有 A 才 B is a formal version of 只有……才……
q: What does the cocoon metaphor suggest?
People are wrapped in their own preferences

L.s: Retelling of a story from Romance of the Three Kingdoms (public domain)
L.su: Zhuge Liang outwits his rival with fog and straw.
ss: In the Three Kingdoms period, Zhou Yu was deeply jealous of Zhuge Liang's talent and kept looking for a chance to get rid of him.
One day Zhou Yu said to Zhuge Liang, "Can you make a hundred thousand arrows within ten days?"
Zhuge Liang replied calmly, "Three days is enough. If I fail, I will gladly accept punishment."
Zhou Yu was secretly delighted, thinking Zhuge Liang would certainly fail this time.
Zhuge Liang, however, quietly borrowed twenty boats from Lu Su and filled each with straw figures.
Before dawn on the third day, thick fog covered the river.
Zhuge Liang ordered the boats towards Cao Cao's camp, beating drums and shouting as if to attack.
Cao Cao feared an ambush and dared not fight, only ordering his soldiers to shoot arrows at the river.
Before the sun rose, the straw figures were covered with arrows, and Zhuge Liang had "borrowed" over a hundred thousand.
Hearing of it, Zhou Yu sighed deeply, "I am no match for him!"
g: Reply to me within a week.
q: What did Zhou Yu ask Zhuge Liang to do?
What did Zhuge Liang put on the boats?
Why did Cao Cao shoot arrows?
He feared an ambush in the fog

L.su: "Clear waters and green mountains are mountains of gold and silver."
ss: "Clear waters and green mountains are mountains of gold and silver" has become the concept of China's ecological civilisation.
Its meaning: protecting the ecology protects productivity, and improving it develops productivity.

In the past some places, in pursuit of growth, did not hesitate to sacrifice the environment, with the result that land desertified, rivers were polluted and air quality worsened, in turn restraining development.
After a painful reflection, localities began adjusting industrial structure, closing heavily polluting firms and vigorously developing clean energy and eco-tourism.
The builders of the Saihanba forest farm planted trees for decades as one day, turning a wasteland into a million-mu sea of forest.
Today it is not only a green barrier for the capital but attracts many visitors.
Practice proves economic development and environmental protection are not in conflict; the key is finding a sustainable path.
g: 不惜 means "not hesitate to (at cost)".
He would pay any price to save people.
痛定思痛 is a chengyu: "reflect on a painful lesson".
Having reflected painfully, he decided to change.
q: Green mountains with gold and silver
What is the key to harmony of growth and ecology?

L.su: Where convenience ends and surveillance begins.
ss: The footprints we leave online each day are being collected, analysed and used on an unprecedented scale.
Merchants use big data to target ads, which raises marketing efficiency but also makes consumers feel their every move is watched.
More seriously, once personal information leaks it may be used by criminals for fraud, causing irreparable loss.
To meet this challenge, countries have enacted laws strengthening the protection of personal information, explicitly requiring firms to obtain users' clear consent before collecting data.
But the improvement of law often lags behind technology; many users click "agree" without really reading long, obscure privacy terms.
Clearly protecting privacy cannot depend on legislation alone; firms must keep faith and users raise self-protection awareness, forming a pattern of shared governance.
Seeking balance between convenience and privacy will be a long-term task in the digital age.
g: 固然 concedes a point before a "but".
价格固然重要，质量也不能忽视。
Price matters, but quality can't be ignored.
q: What do merchants use big data for?
What is the problem with privacy terms?

L.s: Tang poem by Li Bai (public domain)
L.su: Li Bai sails swiftly down the Yangtze after being pardoned.
ss: At dawn I left Baidi among the rosy clouds;
a thousand li to Jiangling, and back in a single day.
The monkeys on both banks cried without cease,
while my light boat passed ten thousand mountains.

L.s: Tang poem by Li Bai (public domain)
L.te: Gazing at the Waterfall on Mount Lu
L.su: Li Bai imagines the Milky Way tumbling from heaven.
ss: Sunlight on Incense Burner Peak raises purple mist;
from afar the waterfall hangs before the river.
Flying down straight for three thousand feet,

L.su: Confucius on learning from everyone you meet.

Pick out their good qualities and follow them;
their bad qualities — correct in yourself.
q: What can you learn from others?
What do you do with their flaws?

L.s: Song poem by Lu You (public domain)
L.su: Lu You's dying wish for a reunited country.

On the day the royal army pacifies the Central Plains in the north,
at the family rites, don't forget to tell your father.

L.s: Tang poem by Du Fu (public domain)
L.su: Du Fu, in a ruined capital, sees spring return to a broken land.
ss: The state is broken, yet mountains and rivers remain;
spring in the city — grass and trees grow thick.
Moved by the times, flowers splash me with tears;
hating parting, birds startle my heart.
Beacon fires have lasted three months;
a letter from home is worth ten thousand gold.
I scratch my white hair and it grows shorter,
hardly able to hold a hairpin.
q: What remains although the state is broken?
What is a letter from home worth?
What is happening to his hair?

L.s: Tang poem by Wang Wei (public domain)

ss: The empty mountain shows no one,
yet voices echo faintly.
Returning sunlight enters the deep forest
and shines again upon the green moss.

L.su: A grassland song from the northern steppes.

The sky is like a dome tent, covering the fields on all sides.
Sky so blue, field so vast;
when the wind bends the grass, cattle and sheep come into view.

L.su: Confucius on learning, friendship and not minding being unrecognised.
ss: The Master said: To learn and then to practise it in due time, is that not a pleasure?
To have friends come from afar, is that not a joy?
To be unrecognised by others yet feel no resentment, is that not a gentleman?
q: What does Confucius say is a pleasure?

L.s: Han poem by Cao Cao (public domain)
L.su: Cao Cao stands on a cliff and imagines the sea holding sun, moon and stars.
ss: Eastward I reach Jieshi to gaze at the vast sea.
How the waters ripple, the island peaks rise tall.
Trees grow in clusters, a hundred grasses flourish.
Autumn wind sighs; great waves surge up.
The sun and moon in their courses seem to rise from within it;
the bright Milky Way seems to come from inside it.
How fortunate indeed — I sing to express my aim.

What seems to come from the sea?

L.su: Short sayings about learning and thinking.
ss: The Master said: One who revisits the old and learns the new is fit to be a teacher.
Learning without thinking is confusing; thinking without learning is dangerous.
To know what you know and to know what you do not know: that is knowledge.
q: What makes someone fit to be a teacher?
Revisiting the old and learning the new
What happens if you learn without thinking?
Knowing what you do and don't know

L.s: Tang poem by Liu Zongyuan (public domain)
L.su: Liu Zongyuan paints a lonely old fisherman in the snow.

on ten thousand paths no footprints remain.
A lone boat, an old man in a straw cape and hat,

What does the old man wear?

L.s: Retelling of a traditional Chinese folk tale
L.te: The Cowherd and the Weaver Girl
L.su: The love story behind the Qixi Festival.
ss: Long ago there was a lonely young man who lived by herding cattle; people called him the Cowherd.
His only property was an old ox, which was in fact the Golden Ox Star come down from heaven.
One day the ox told him that the heavenly maidens would bathe at the lake and that if he took one of the garments he would gain a wife.
The Cowherd did so, and the garment he took was the Weaver Girl's.
The Weaver Girl became his wife, and they lived happily and had a son and a daughter.
But the Queen Mother flew into a rage when she found out and sent heavenly soldiers to seize the Weaver Girl.

The Cowherd carried his children in baskets and chased her wearing the ox hide; just as he was about to catch up, the Queen Mother drew a golden hairpin and carved the roaring Milky Way across the sky.
Thousands upon thousands of magpies, moved by their love, fly up on the seventh day of the seventh month each year to form a bridge over the Milky Way and let them meet.
g: 眼看 means "just about to; before one's eyes".
勃然大怒 is a four-character idiom: "flare up in anger".
Hearing the news he flew into a rage.
q: What did the Cowherd do for a living?
What helps them meet each year?

L.su: Two sides haggle over delivery dates and penalties.
ss: We've seen your quotation. Overall acceptable, but the delivery deadline still needs discussion.
By when would you like delivery?
No later than the fifteenth of next month, otherwise our production plan will be delayed.
I'm afraid that's difficult. Raw material procurement takes long; the earliest is month-end.
Then the contract should specify liability for late delivery — for example, one percent of payment deducted per day of delay.
That clause is too harsh. We propose 0.5 percent, plus a force-majeure exemption clause.
0.5 percent is possible, but the scope of the exemption must be defined clearly to avoid later disputes.
No problem. We'll have legal draft a supplementary agreement and sign and seal once both confirm.
g: 以免 means "so as to avoid".
Set off early so as not to be late.
q: What does Party A object to?
What does Party B propose for penalties?

L.te: The Meaning of the Spring Festival
L.su: Why the Lunar New Year remains the heart of Chinese family life.
ss: The Spring Festival is China's most solemn traditional holiday, its history traceable to sacrificial rites over three thousand years ago.

About its origin, a folk legend tells of the "Nian beast": every New Year's Eve a fierce monster came out to harm people and livestock, and people discovered it feared red and loud noise, so they pasted red couplets and set off firecrackers to drive it away.
These customs have continued to this day, symbolising seeing off the old and welcoming the new, and warding off evil and disaster.
On New Year's Eve the whole family sits together for the reunion dinner; northerners are used to making dumplings while southerners like making rice cake, each with its own customs.
Elders give children red envelopes, hoping the young will spend the new year safely.
In recent years, as life speeds up, some young people choose "cloud greetings", greeting relatives and friends by video.
Though the form is changing, the meaning of reunion remains constant.
During the annual Spring Festival travel rush, hundreds of millions cross mountains and rivers to go home, just to share this special night with loved ones.
g: 这座寺庙的历史可以追溯到唐朝。
This temple's history can be traced to the Tang.
始终如一 is an idiom: "consistent from beginning to end".
q: What did the Nian beast fear?

L.su: From oracle bones to simplified characters.
ss: Chinese characters are among the world's oldest scripts, with a history of over three thousand years.
The earliest mature writing so far discovered is the Shang dynasty oracle-bone script, so called because it was carved on tortoise shells and animal bones.
Later the script developed in turn into bronze script, great seal and small seal.
After Qin Shi Huang unified China, he ordered the script unified and made small seal the standard.
By the Han dynasty clerical script gradually became popular, writing became more convenient, and the shape of characters changed from round to square.
The regular script that appeared afterwards has been used until today and became the basis of modern characters.
In the 1950s mainland China promoted simplified characters, reducing strokes and making them easier to learn and use.
Taiwan, Hong Kong and some other places still use traditional characters today.
g: 是……的 stresses how, when or where something happened (as in 它是刻在龟甲和兽骨上的).
Please enter the classroom in turn.
q: What is the earliest mature script mentioned?
Which places still use traditional characters?

L.su: Why standard speech and local tongues need each other.
ss: China is vast and has many dialects; roughly divided, there are seven major dialect regions: Mandarin, Wu, Yue, Min, Hakka, Xiang and Gan.
The differences are so large that people from different regions often cannot converse directly; even two districts of one city may have different accents.
Promoting Mandarin has removed barriers to cross-regional communication and powerfully advanced education and economic development.
However, as Mandarin spreads, some dialects are quietly vanishing, especially among the young, fewer of whom speak authentic dialect.
A dialect is not only a tool for communication but also carries a region's historical memory and local customs.
Many classical poems rhyme better when read in Cantonese or Hokkien, because those dialects preserve many features of ancient pronunciation.
Protecting dialects therefore does not mean denying Mandarin; the two can complement each other and coexist harmoniously.
g: 相辅相成 is a chengyu: "complement each other".
Theory and practice complement each other.
q: How many major dialect regions are listed?
Why do ancient poems rhyme better in some dialects?

L.su: How livestreaming became a new kind of shopping mall.
ss: In recent years "livestream selling" has become a new sales model sweeping the country.
Hosts introduce goods while interacting in real time with viewers, stimulating the desire to buy.
For farmers, livestreaming has opened sales channels for produce; specialities from remote areas have thus entered countless households.
Yet the industry's boom also bred chaos: exaggerated claims, false sales and faked data are common.
Many consumers ordered on impulse and found after receipt that the quality fell far short of the advertising.
In response, regulators issued rules requiring hosts to describe goods truthfully and punishing violations severely.
In the long run, only by returning to the goods themselves and winning reputation through quality can this model last.
g: 屡见不鲜 is a chengyu: "commonly seen".
q: What does the host do while selling?
Interacts with viewers in real time

L.te: Daodejing: A Journey of a Thousand Miles
L.su: Laozi on great things growing from small beginnings.
ss: A tree too big to embrace grows from a tiny shoot;
a nine-storey tower rises from piled earth;
a journey of a thousand miles begins beneath the feet.
q: Where does a big tree start?
What is a tower built from?
Where does a long journey begin?

L.s: Song poem by Su Shi (public domain)
L.su: Su Shi, on Mid-Autumn night, wonders about the moon and longs for his brother.
ss: When did the bright moon first appear?
Cup in hand, I ask the blue sky.
I do not know, in the palaces of heaven,
what year it is tonight.
I wish to ride the wind and return there,
yet I fear those jade towers and crystal halls
are too cold to bear up high.
I rise and dance with my clear shadow;
how can that compare with being among men?
I only wish that we may live long,
and share the beauty of the moon, though a thousand miles apart.
q: What does the poet fear in heaven?
It is too cold up high
What does the last line wish for?
To share the moon from afar

L.su: Liu Yuxi finds dignity in a plain study.
ss: A mountain need not be high; with an immortal it becomes famous.
Water need not be deep; with a dragon it becomes divine.
This is a humble room, but my virtue makes it fragrant.
Moss traces climb the steps in green; grass colour enters the blinds in blue.
Great scholars laugh and talk here; no commoners come and go.
q: How does the poet describe his room?

L.su: Xunzi on how steady effort accomplishes great things.
ss: Blue is taken from the indigo plant, yet is bluer than indigo;
ice is made of water, yet is colder than water.
Without accumulating small steps, you cannot reach a thousand miles;
without gathering small streams, you cannot form rivers and seas.
If you give up carving, even rotten wood cannot be snapped;
if you keep carving, even metal and stone can be engraved.
q: What does 青出于蓝 suggest?
A student can surpass the teacher
What is needed to travel a thousand miles?

L.te: Daodejing: The Highest Good Is Like Water
L.su: Laozi praises water for benefiting all things without competing.
ss: The highest good is like water.
Water benefits all things and does not compete;
it settles in places that people despise, and so comes close to the Way.
In dwelling, be good at choosing the ground; in heart, be deep; in giving, be kind; in speech, be trustworthy;
in government, be orderly; in affairs, be capable; in action, be timely.
Only because it does not compete is it free from blame.
q: What is the highest good compared with?
Why is water free from blame?

L.s: Zhou Dunyi, Ai Lian Shuo (public domain)
L.su: Zhou Dunyi praises the lotus as a gentleman among flowers.
ss: I alone love the lotus: rising from mud yet unstained,
washed in clear ripples yet not coquettish,
hollow within and straight without, with no tendrils or branches,
its fragrance far-reaching and ever purer, standing tall and clean,
to be viewed from afar but not handled playfully.
q: Where does the lotus grow from?

L.s: Qing poem by Gong Zizhen (public domain)
L.su: Gong Zizhen calls on Heaven to send talent of every kind.
ss: The nine regions' vitality depends on wind and thunder;
ten thousand horses all silent — this is truly sad.
I urge Heaven to rouse itself again,
and send down talent without limiting its mould.
q: What does the poet find sad?

L.su: Why preserving the past and building the new are not enemies.
ss: In today's fast-developing society, the relationship between tradition and innovation is often misread as an either-or opposition.
Some believe that holding to tradition means resting on one's laurels and refusing progress; others fear that blindly pursuing innovation will pull culture up by its roots.
In fact, both views are one-sided.
No innovation can arise from nothing; it is bound to emerge from the experience and wisdom accumulated by predecessors.
Conversely, a tradition lacking innovation will eventually lose vitality and decline into a museum exhibit.

Take Chinese calligraphy: for centuries calligraphers both copied the classics and kept seeking change, which created a scene where seal, clerical, regular, running and cursive scripts vied in splendour.
True inheritance is not preserving things unchanged, but giving them new meaning for the age on the basis of understanding their inner spirit.
As the saying goes, "reviewing the old to know the new" — only by deeply understanding the past can we face the future more calmly.
g: 非此即彼 means "either this or that".
以 A 为例 means "take A as an example".
以北京为例，交通问题很严重。
Take Beijing: its traffic problem is serious.
q: What happens to tradition without innovation?

L.te: The Artistic Mood of Chinese Landscape Painting
L.su: Why empty space matters in ink painting.
ss: Unlike Western painting's pursuit of realism, Chinese landscape painting emphasises the painter's inner feelings and spiritual realm.
Painters do not cling to faithful depiction; they take in the myriad things of nature, refine and select, then express their feelings with brush and ink.
This is the so-called "intent before the brush".
In composition, landscape painting values blank space: an empty area can be mist, a river, or the world imagined by the viewer.
Because of this clever contrast of emptiness and substance, the picture seems ethereal, far-reaching and thought-provoking.
Yuan painter Huang Gongwang's "Dwelling in the Fuchun Mountains" depicts the lovely scenery of the Fuchun River in subtle ink, and is hailed as one of China's ten great surviving paintings.
Viewing such a work feels like standing among mountains and waters, with the soul cleansed.
g: 这部电影的结尾耐人寻味。
拘泥于 means "to stick rigidly to".

L.su: Han Yu defines what a teacher is for.
ss: Scholars of old always had teachers.
A teacher is one who transmits the Way, imparts learning and resolves doubts.
People are not born knowing — who can be without doubt?
If one has doubts but does not follow a teacher, those doubts will never be resolved.
q: Transmit the Way and resolve doubts

L.te: Zhuangzi: Zhuang Zhou Dreams of a Butterfly
L.su: Was the dreamer a man dreaming a butterfly, or a butterfly dreaming a man?
ss: Once Zhuang Zhou dreamed he was a butterfly,
a fluttering, lively butterfly indeed;
content with itself, it did not know it was Zhou.
Suddenly he woke, and was solidly Zhou again.
He knew not whether Zhou had dreamed the butterfly, or the butterfly dreamed Zhou.
Between Zhou and the butterfly there must be a distinction.
This is called the transformation of things.
q: What did Zhuang Zhou dream he was?
What does the story call this?

L.s: Fan Zhongyan, Yueyang Lou Ji (public domain)
L.su: Fan Zhongyan's famous statement of public duty.
ss: Not delighted by outward things, not saddened by one's own lot.
High in the court, one worries for the people;
far away on rivers and lakes, one worries for the ruler.
So advancing brings worry, and retreating brings worry too.
Then when is one happy?
Surely one will say: be first to worry about the world's worries, and last to enjoy the world's joys!
q: Who does one worry for when at court?
What is the closing maxim about?
Worrying before the world and enjoying after
What should one not be moved by?

CY: draw a snake and add feet
To ruin something by adding what it does not need.
In a story from the Warring States Strategies, men raced to draw a snake. The first to finish added feet, so his snake no longer counted as a snake, and he lost the prize of wine.
The article is already clear. Adding another paragraph would only spoil it.
wait by a stump for a hare
To wait for luck instead of making an effort.
The philosopher Han Feizi told of a farmer who saw a hare run into a tree stump and die. He gave up farming to wait by the stump for more hares.
If you want to succeed, you cannot sit and wait for luck. You have to work.
mend the pen after a sheep is lost
It is not too late to fix a problem, even after a loss.
A minister told the king of Chu that a man who mends his pen after losing a sheep can still save the rest of his flock.
You did badly on this exam, but if you fix your study now, it is not too late.
play the lute to an ox
To speak to someone who cannot understand.
The oxen in the old tale hear the music but cannot appreciate it. The idiom is often used with humour, or with a little scorn.
He knows nothing about music, so talking to him about it is like playing the lute to an ox.
the frog at the bottom of a well
A person with a narrow view of the world.
In the Zhuangzi, a frog in a well thinks the sky is only as big as the round opening above it, until a turtle from the sea tells it about the ocean.
Go out and see more, and do not be a frog in a well.
the fox borrows the tiger's might
To bully others by using a powerful person's name.
In the Strategies of the Warring States, a fox that was caught by a tiger told it to walk behind and watch the animals run. They ran from the tiger, not from the fox.
He is only the manager's friend, but he throws his weight around at his colleagues.
the bow in the cup looks like a snake
To be afraid of something that is not there.
A man drank wine and saw a snake in his cup. He fell ill from fear, until he learned it was only the reflection of a bow hanging on the wall.
She is scared by every little sound, as if she saw a snake in every cup.
a tiger's head and a snake's tail
A strong start and a weak finish.
Used for plans, projects and books that begin with a lot of energy and then fade away.
He always starts a task with energy and then loses interest.
To stand out clearly from the crowd.
Used as a compliment, often about someone's height or talent.
He is tall and handsome and stands out in the crowd.
To achieve two goals with one action.
A general of the Northern dynasties was said to have shot two eagles with a single arrow. It is the Chinese cousin of "killing two birds with one stone".
Cycling to work is exercise and saves money, which kills two birds with one stone.
success arrives as soon as the horse does
A traditional good-luck wish, popular at the start of a new business or a journey.
I wish you quick success in your new job!
not even a crow or sparrow makes a sound
Used for rooms and crowds that suddenly go quiet.
As soon as the teacher walked in, the classroom went silent.
A tiny part of something large.
The historian Sima Qian used it to say that his own death would count for no more than a hair on nine oxen.
This little money is a drop in the ocean for him.
like a fish that has found water
In the Three Kingdoms period, Liu Bei said he was like a fish that had found water after he met the strategist Zhuge Liang.
At the new company he is in his element and enjoys the work.
an old horse knows the way
An experienced person can show the way.
Han Feizi tells how an army lost its way and followed old horses, which led it home.
He has walked this road for twenty years, so he knows it like an old horse.
keep your mouth shut like a bottle
A bottle with its cap on lets nothing out. It is often used for official secrets and private matters.
Please keep this matter strictly to yourself.
To gain two things with one action.
A common way to praise a clever plan.
Working abroad earns money and teaches a language, so you gain two things at once.
Used to criticise someone who cannot give one thing their full attention.
Do not be half-hearted when you study.
The numbers describe a heart that jumps up and down like buckets in a well.
While I waited for my exam results, I felt very nervous.
Often used for accidents, wars and serious illness.
He barely survived the earthquake, and now he is fine.
ten parts complete, ten parts beautiful
Often used in the negative: nothing in this world is perfect.
Nobody in this world is perfect.
Of every kind; a great variety.
The phrase first described changing military formations. Now it means a wide range of things.
The drinks in the supermarket are so varied that I do not know which to buy.
Used for work, study and love alike.
He looks after his sick mother with all his heart.
a thousand methods and a hundred plans
Often used for hard goals that require a lot of effort.
He tried every way he could to get into university.
a hundred shots, a hundred hits
To hit the target every time.
The archer Yang Youji of the Spring and Autumn period was famous for hitting a willow leaf from a hundred paces. Now it is used for shooting, sports and predictions.
He never misses a shot at basketball.
To fall in love at first sight.
钟情 means to give one's love.
They fell in love at first sight at a friend's wedding.
ten thousand times without one mistake
This method is completely safe, so do not worry.
Used for repeated actions, often annoying ones.
I reminded him again and again, but he still forgot.
A very common good-luck wish for studies, work and travel.
Used for crowds and voices that come from every side.
The people at the contest came from all over.
the Foolish Old Man moves the mountains
With perseverance, even the hardest task can be done.
In an old tale, an old man decided to dig away two mountains in front of his house. When laughed at, he said his sons and grandsons would carry on. Heaven moved the mountains for him.
With the spirit of the Foolish Old Man, nothing is impossible.
an iron rod becomes a needle
Legend says the young poet Li Bai met an old woman who was grinding an iron rod into a needle. He understood that persistence pays off and went back to his books.
Learning characters takes patience, like grinding an iron rod into a needle.
Small efforts, kept up, can achieve great things.
A drop of water is weak, but drop after drop wears through a rock.
Read for ten minutes a day, and after a year you will have improved a great deal.
hold on to it with constancy
Often said about exercise, study and good habits.
The most important thing in learning a language is to keep at it.
give up sleep and forget meals
To be so absorbed that one forgets to eat or sleep.
Used as praise for hard workers, or with a smile for people who are hooked on a game.
He studied day and night, forgetting to eat and sleep, to prepare for the exam.
bore through the wall to borrow light
To study hard in spite of poverty.
The Han-dynasty scholar Kuang Heng was too poor to buy candles. He made a hole in the wall to read by the light of his neighbour's house.
The old story of boring through the wall shows that poverty need not stop anyone from studying.
tie hair to a beam, prick the thigh
Two scholars, Sun Jing and Su Qin, were said to keep themselves awake at night like this. It describes hard study.
To get into university, he studies as hard as the scholars of old.
Used to encourage people who feel stuck while learning a skill.
Do not worry. Practice makes perfect, so keep trying.
To learn many things from one example.
Confucius said he would only teach a student who could work out the other three corners after being shown one.
A good student can infer other cases and does not just memorise answers.
review the old to learn the new
To gain new insight by reviewing the past.
This line comes from the Analects of Confucius.
Reviewing old lessons is also a way to find something new.
To always try to do better.
Used for crafts, products and skills.
The chef at this restaurant always tries to improve every dish.
The idiom often appears in the advice that one should never give up halfway.
You must not give up halfway.
It has two meanings. As an answer to "How are you?" or "How was it?", it means "so-so". About a task, it means careless.
He does his homework carelessly, so he makes many mistakes.
Praise for people who do detailed work with great care.
